title: Comfort Club Dues Ledger: Payment Application, Past-Due Status, Late Fees and Termination
content:
Billing office rules for the dues ledger of Comfort Club Maintenance Agreements.

## Payments and activation
- A payment is applied to the agreement's oldest unpaid charge first, then to the next oldest.
- A pending agreement becomes active on the day the payment covering its first dues charge posts.
- An enrollment whose first dues charge is still unpaid on the tier's nonpayment termination day after it posted is closed from pending to cancelled.

## Past-due status and the late fee
- An agreement is moved to past due only once a dues charge has stayed unpaid for **more than** the tier's payment grace days, counted in calendar days after the dues charge was posted.
- Grace and termination days are counted as calendar days from the day after the posting date: day 1 is the day after the charge posts.
- Moving to past due posts a late fee at the tier's late fee amount for that billing month. Only one late fee is charged per unpaid billing month.
- A payment that clears every overdue charge and fee returns the agreement to active on the day it posts.
- While an agreement is past due its member benefits are suspended: no tune-up is booked, no covered repair is drawn and no response-guarantee credit is earned until it is active again.

## Termination for nonpayment
An agreement still holding a dues charge unpaid the tier's nonpayment termination days after that charge was posted is terminated from past due to cancelled, with no cancellation credit and no cancellation fee; its unpaid charges remain owed.

## Late fee waivers
- A late fee may be waived only while the number of late fee waiver credits posted to the agreement in the 12 months before the waiver date is below the tier's waiver allowance. The 12 months run back from the date of handling; the same calendar date one year earlier is not inside them.
- A waiver credits the full late fee, names that fee as its source, and is never granted on a late fee that has already been waived.
- A tier with a waiver allowance of zero never waives late fees.

## Counting the grace period (hypothetical dates, 15-day grace)

| Charge posted | Date | Day count | Still unpaid that day — past due? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 March | 16 March | day 15 | No (15 days is not more than 15) |
| 1 March | 17 March | day 16 | Yes; the late fee for that billing month posts |

On a 60-day termination period, a charge posted on 1 March and still unpaid on day 60 (30 April) leads to termination as described above.

## Waiver allowance check (hypothetical, allowance of 1)

| Waiver credits posted in the 12 months before the waiver date | Waiver possible? |
|---|---|
| 0 | Yes — 0 is below 1 |
| 1 | No — 1 is not below 1 |
